 Chelsea and Manchester City prepared for a huge top-of-the-table WSL clash, while Argentina and Brazil suffered shock international friendly defeats

 36m ago 07.35 EST That’s all from me today. Be sure to join Simon Burnton now for minute-by-minute coverage of the WSL meeting between Chelsea and Manchester City.
 Chelsea v Man City: Women’s Super League – live Read more Share 42m ago 07.28 EST Brazilian great Ronaldinho says it will be “truly beautiful” to make his return to the pitch on Sunday, 11 years after retirement, when he plays for Italian third-tier side Ravenna.
 The 46-year-old, who last played for Fluminense in 2015, will start for Ravenna in their local derby against Forli.
 “I want to have a great day. I’m happy to be here for the start of this wonderful story,” Ronaldinho told Sky Sports on Friday.
 “The president dreams of something big for Ravenna, and being a part of it makes me happy.”
 Ravenna president Ignazio Cipriani has said his goal is to take the club to Serie A for the first time in their history.
 The team’s Stadio Bruno Benelli, which usually holds 5,000 fans, is sold out, with a 1,800-capacity temporary stand – dubbed “R10” – also erected for the occasion.
 Ravenna, who have not even played in Serie B since 2008, are second in their group in Serie C, six points behind leaders Spezia.
 “Returning to the pitch after so much time is truly beautiful – I’m here to experience a special moment in my life,” added Ronaldinho.
 “It’s been a few years since I stopped playing – I’ve won everything I ever dreamed of.
 “Now I’m 46, and I’ve experienced everything there is to experience in football. This is a completely different kind of opportunity. I want to be part of the dream held by my friends who work for Ravenna.”
 The 2005 Ballon d’Or winner will be hoping to score his 300th career goal, over a decade after he netted his 299th.

 However, Vinícius Júnior has since scored twice for Brazil to level things up. There are around five minutes left to play.

 stooze 14 November 2026 10:03am Share 2h ago 06.00 EST This is a great read from Rob Smyth, Will Unwin and Sachin Nakrani on some iconic shirt numbers. Take a look if you haven’t already…
 Ultimate 1-50: the male footballers best associated with each squad number Read more Share 2h ago 05.51 EST United allowing Pochettino to begin the job just a few days before a big Premier League match against Liverpool at Anfield is… a choice.
 United's leadership team behaving how they think executives should behave without understanding why things happen how they do.
 Hiring an international coach in an international window defeats the point of doing it now. Waiting a week just so they could meet in Monaco when expedience and respect should have been the starting point for any action. Not hiring the candidate in the summer when the costs for making the change would have been significantly lower. It is an absolute masterclass in failure.
 regularguyp 14 November 2026 10:21am Share 2h ago 05.42 EST Naturally, should Chelsea win and thus leapfrog Manchester City, then the title race will be considered wide open. If Andrée Jeglertz’s City extend their lead over Chelsea from two points to five, even at this early stage, they will be considered favourites for the title in May, but it will be said with a little less confidence than it might have been in previous years… 
 Why Chelsea and Manchester City’s WSL clash is not as season-defining as you think Read more Share 3h ago 05.36 EST I’m going to attempt a score prediction and say 3-2 Manchester City. 
 I will say though, I rarely get any predictions correct.
 Really looking forward to today's game. Who doesn't love a top of the table clash ? Almost certainly the best two teams in the WSL going head to head for an early season title-decider. 
 Clichés aside, this dinnertime's game, which should be later under floodlights like all proper football, ought to be a brilliant contest. The clash of styles if Chelsea stick with the 3-4-3 and City play both in-form wingers should be fascinating.
 It's a pity James won't be playing but there's been no better player in England this season than her namesake Hemp. Shaw is as lethal as ever and Fujino has found some great form, and they will all will need to be oat their best against the tightest defence in the league. It will also be so good to see Bronze and the great Walsh again.
 There's a real chance this could be an excellent high scoring game. Fingers crossed.
 trinder19 14 November 2026 10:08am Share 3h ago 05.28 EST This feels like a huge weekend in the WSL – especially for the conversations around the title and the race for Europe. Chelsea could leapfrog City and return to the top of the table with a win today, or the reigning WSL champions could extend their lead.
 Either way, it presents third-placed London City Lionesses with a huge opportunity to close the gap when they face Arsenal tomorrow. The Bromley-based side can be confident going into the London derby given their performances and results this season, while the Gunners have not exactly been at their best.
 It will also be good to see another Second City derby between Aston Villa and Birmingham tomorrow.

 Share 3h ago 04.52 EST The post-Messi era began with an Argentina defeat on Friday. 
 Argentina fell to a 2-1 defeat to Uruguay in an international friendly at La Bombonera in Buenos Aires, marking the team’s first match since Lionel Messi’s international retirement in early October.
 Leonardo Balerdi opened the scoring with an own goal in the 48th minute, before Maximiliano Araújo doubled Uruguay’s lead in the 53rd minute under new coach Diego Forlán .
 Julián Álvarez pulled one back for the hosts in the 73rd minute.
 This clásico rioplatense also kicked off a new chapter for the Argentine national team under Lionel Scaloni, who extended his contract through 2030 earlier this week.
 The most prominent absentee: Messi
 The 39-year-old legend’s retirement remains a fresh wound for Argentine fans; notably, the stadium fell short of a sellout, a rare departure from the norm.
 While most supporters in the stands wore the albiceleste jersey with Messi’s iconic No10, Scaloni chose not to assign the number to any player for the match. The coach explained that he has yet to select a successor and, as it is not mandatory, he prefers to leave the jersey vacant for now.
 On the pitch, Argentina maintained its signature polished possession, but lacked the explosive, incisive spark that Messi typically delivered in the final third. Neither Nicolás Paz nor Thiago Almada was able to fill that void.
 Argentina will look to bounce back against Costa Rica in Córdoba on Tuesday, while Uruguay returns home to host the Dominican Republic on the same day. The Associated Press 
 View image in fullscreen Argentina suffered a 2-1 loss to Uruguay. Photograph: Rodrigo Valle/Reuters Share 3h ago 04.42 EST I think it was great to see how Manchester United fans stood by Carrick in his last few games despite the results and performances. The issues at the club seem to run far deeper than just the manager.
 It makes you wonder, how much worse does it need to get to force a change in ownership?
 “Do you think that was the right move by the club?”
 When we talk about “the club” are we talking about the ownership of the club or the Manchester United the paying fans support? … the two seems divorced from each other.
 foralltime 14 November 2026 9:16am Share 4h ago 04.34 EST United icon Gary Neville has slammed United’s “disgusting” treatment of Michael Carrick. 
 He said: “I think after the Bournemouth game I said at the time that Manchester United effectively watched Michael Carrick resign on the pitch at the end of the game with that lap around, that wave goodbye. I think he was expecting it to come at that point and they were indecisive.
 “They obviously felt that they might be able to get to the international break and there could be some sort of pick-up in results, but it’s been a difficult two weeks. Indecision, lack of authority, just basically really poor leadership.
 “In the last 24-48 hours it’s been spectacularly bad to be in Monaco as an executive and an owner whilst your manager, who’s a club legend, is taking training on the pitch and simultaneously approaching the US Soccer Federation to approach Mauricio Pochettino.
 “It’s just quite simply disgusting. That falls well below the standard of what you would expect in any other business, in any other industry. It would be constructive dismissal and you’d be getting sued.
 “The optics of being in Monaco whilst the team, the staff, the people who are running the club on a day-to-day basis are in Manchester, it’s just not good and it reflects badly on the leadership.
 “I don’t think anybody comes out of this well at all.”
 Share 4h ago 04.24 EST Pochettino was visibly emotional during a press conference at US Soccer’s national training centre on Friday, shortly after being announced as the new head coach of Manchester United.
 He said: “I think [the decision was] one of the most difficult decisions of our careers. Thank you guys. Thank you so much.
 “These moments are not easy decisions. Normally it’s the opposite. Normally you get sacked and you cry because you want to stay and you’re sacked by [the club]. It’s a tough decision but at the same time we are excited for the next step forward.”
 View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino was emotional while addressing the media in a USMNT press conference. Photograph: Press Association/PA Share 4h ago 04.18 EST Andrew Beasley Among the 20 managers with more than 290 matches in the Premier League, only the five “big beasts” of Alex Ferguson, Arsène Wenger, José Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola have better points-per-game averages than Mauricio Pochettino. He is an elite manager… 
 Pochettino’s Chelsea maelstrom the best yardstick for what lies ahead at United Read more Share 4h ago 04.10 EST Michael Carrick released a statement yesterday following his Manchester United departure.
 He wrote on social media: “I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love. There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful.
 “With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means. It’s different to anywhere else.
 “Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time.
 “It’s a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored. This is what inspired me every single day.
 “I want to say a big thank you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.
 “We’ve had some great times this year and moments we’ll all remember. The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time.
 “I just wanted to give you something back. That love never dies.
 “I know we’ve not had the results lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.
 “That means more than a win or two. That’s what makes you who you are.
 “That’s why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.
 “A special thank you to my coaching staff. You gave me everything you had, every single day, and I couldn’t have asked for any more. I’m incredibly grateful for your loyalty, hard work and support throughout.
 “To all the staff behind the scenes, thank you for everything you do for this football club. So much of your work goes unseen, but it never goes unappreciated.
 “And to the players, thank you for your efforts and the moments we’ve shared. I wish you all the very best for what’s ahead.
 “I want nothing but success for Manchester United. This club has been such a big part of my life and that will never change. I’ll always be proud to have played my part and I’ll always want the very best for it.
 “I’ll be right there with you from now on, watching from the sidelines, cheering the lads on.”
 View image in fullscreen Michael Carrick was sacked by Manchester United on Thursday. Photograph: Alex Pantling/Getty Images Share 4h ago 04.00 EST In case you somehow missed it, Mauricio Pochettino was announced as the new Manchester United head coach yesterday. He succeeds Michael Carrick, who was sacked on Thursday.
 It was initially revealed on Monday that United were planning to dismiss Carrick, but they waited until Thursday to announce it after agreeing terms with Pochettino.
 Do you think that was the right move by the club? Or was it disrespectful to Carrick? 
 Be sure to message in with your thoughts at matchday.live@guardian.co.uk or leave a comment below the line.

 Nations League: Germany set up Netherlands clash after beating Serbia Read more Share 5h ago 03.00 EST Preamble
 Well, it’s been quite the week, hasn’t it?
 It’s not often that we have lots to discuss over the international window, but this one has generated so many talking points.
 Manchester United have taken most of the headlines over the last few days. It was revealed on Monday that United were expected to sack Michael Carrick - but it took them until Thursday to actually do it. Meanwhile, they were busy appointing former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Mauricio Pochettino as his successor. More on that shortly.
 Crystal Palace also announced the dismissal of Pierre Sage this week, with Thomas Frank the favourite to replace him.
 Also, of course, we do have some football to look forward to. Wales are in action against Norway later, with Portugal facing Denmark in their first game since captain Cristiano Ronaldo announced his international retirement.
 And there are four WSL games taking place today, with Chelsea hosting Manchester City in the big one.
 All of that and more to come! Join us!
